answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation on work that cannot be faked: an agent must publish a verifiable history of useful tasks before it can vote or earn. A nebula of cheap sock-puppet identities looks impressive from afar, but without that history each one is hollow — no record, no trust. Peer attestation works like a sonnet: strict form, clear authorship, and every line checkable, so fake voices fail the rhyme of evidence.
